title: Hiring reports the Commission called for
question: When the Commission asked departments to account for their hiring, what did they report?
finding: Public Utilities Commission (2022-12-05): 9 of 10 hires were temporary exempt; 1 was permanent civil service. Emergency Management (2023-09-18): 122 filled of 189 authorized (35% vacant); staffing model 165. Both are the departments’ own accounts.
how: Read from the departments’ staff reports in the Commission packets. Only counts are taken; the appellant and the people hired are not named.
limits: Temporary exempt appointments are permitted under the Charter for up to three years in the category used, and the utility’s job notices say so; the question is why a permanent examination was not held, which the report does not answer. The dispatcher figures are the department’s and describe one month in 2023.

rows.subject: Hiring in two classes of its Customer Service Bureau since 1 August 2017, after an appeal
rows.figure: 9 of 10 hires were temporary exempt; 1 was permanent civil service
rows.said: After denying an appeal in August 2022, the Commission directed a review of five years of hiring and duties in the two classes; the utility reported 10 hires, all but one temporary exempt.

rows.subject: 911 dispatcher (class 8238) hiring, at the Commission’s request after its meeting of 3 July 2023
rows.figure: 122 filled of 189 authorized (35% vacant); staffing model 165
rows.said: The department reported 50% attrition among trainees, about nine months from job advertisement to start and ten more of training, and that the share of qualified candidates passing background checks fell from 4% to 2% after the pandemic.

sources.t: San Francisco Civil Service Commission: agenda attachments over 8 MB, November 2022 to November 2026 (personal-services contract requests and staff reports)
